review.noAnswerGiven: You did not answer this question.
review.relatedTitle: Where the passage talks about this
review.pinMatch: You pinned a sentence the answer key cites as evidence.
review.pinMiss: None of your pinned sentences is one the answer key cites as evidence.
review.pinNotGiven: The answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>, so no sentence in the passage confirms or contradicts the statement.

ngInsteadOfFalse.facts: You chose <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. The passage contradicts this statement, so the answer is <en>FALSE</en>. <en>NOT GIVEN</en> would mean the passage gives no information on it.
ngInsteadOfFalse.views: You chose <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. The writer's views contradict this statement, so the answer is <en>NO</en>. <en>NOT GIVEN</en> would mean it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about it.

falseInsteadOfNg.facts: You chose <en>FALSE</en>. The passage gives no information on this: it neither agrees with nor contradicts the statement, so the answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. <en>FALSE</en> would need a sentence that contradicts it.
falseInsteadOfNg.views: You chose <en>NO</en>. It is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this: the passage neither agrees with nor contradicts the statement, so the answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. <en>NO</en> would need the writer's views to contradict it.

ngInsteadOfTrue.facts: You chose <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. The passage agrees with this statement, so the answer is <en>TRUE</en>. <en>NOT GIVEN</en> would mean the passage gives no information on it.
ngInsteadOfTrue.views: You chose <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. The statement agrees with the writer's views, so the answer is <en>YES</en>. <en>NOT GIVEN</en> would mean it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about it.

trueInsteadOfNg.facts: You chose <en>TRUE</en>. The passage gives no information on this: it neither agrees with nor contradicts the statement, so the answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. <en>TRUE</en> would need a sentence that agrees with it.
trueInsteadOfNg.views: You chose <en>YES</en>. It is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this, so the answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>. <en>YES</en> would need the statement to agree with the writer's views.

signals.oneLetterAway: Your answer differs from an accepted answer by one letter.
signals.wordLimit: Your answer has more words than the instruction allows.
signals.notFromPassage: Your answer uses a word that is not in the passage. This task asks for words from the passage.
signals.timeUp: This question had no answer when the time ran out.

retry.title: Your retry
retry.honest: These are questions you have attempted before. This practice result is not an independent measure of your level.
retry.sourceMissing: The attempt these questions came from is no longer on this device.
retry.sourceOldVersion: This test has changed since that attempt, so its questions can't be practised again.
retry.notAllowed: These questions can't be practised from that attempt.

patterns.title: Mistakes that repeated
patterns.scopeThisTry: In this attempt at this test. One test is not enough to show a lasting weakness.
patterns.scopeFirstTry: From your first attempt at this test on this device. Later attempts repeat questions you have worked on before, so they are not used. One test is not enough to show a lasting weakness.
patterns.noneThisTry: Not enough evidence to show a repeated pattern in this attempt.
patterns.noneFirstTry: Not enough evidence to show a repeated pattern in your first attempt at this test.
patterns.unknownFirstTry: We can't tell which was your first try at this test on this device, so we don't look for repeated mistakes in it.
patterns.unavailable: Repeated mistakes can't be shown because this test has changed since your first attempt.

ngFalse.title: <en>NOT GIVEN</en> mixed up with <en>FALSE</en> or <en>NO</en>
ngFalse.count: {count} of {total} questions whose answer was <en>NOT GIVEN</en>, <en>FALSE</en> or <en>NO</en> (questions {numbers})
ngFalse.tip: <en>FALSE</en> or <en>NO</en> means the passage, or the writer's view, contradicts the statement. <en>NOT GIVEN</en> means it neither agrees nor contradicts: the information or the writer's view is not there. Before choosing <en>FALSE</en> or <en>NO</en>, find what contradicts the statement.

ngTrue.title: <en>NOT GIVEN</en> mixed up with <en>TRUE</en> or <en>YES</en>
ngTrue.count: {count} of {total} questions whose answer was <en>NOT GIVEN</en>, <en>TRUE</en> or <en>YES</en> (questions {numbers})
ngTrue.tip: <en>TRUE</en> or <en>YES</en> needs the passage, or the writer's view, to agree with the statement, often in other words. If nothing agrees and nothing contradicts, the answer is <en>NOT GIVEN</en>.

oneLetterAway.title: Possible spelling issues
oneLetterAway.count: {count} of {total} typed answers were one letter away from an accepted answer (questions {numbers})
oneLetterAway.tip: One letter away may be a spelling slip or a different word. In the test, a misspelt answer loses the mark, so copy words from the passage letter by letter.

wordLimit.title: Too many words
wordLimit.count: {count} of {total} typed answers had more words than allowed (questions {numbers})
wordLimit.tip: In the test, an answer with more words than allowed loses the mark. Check the limit in the instruction, for example <en>NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS</en>, and write only the words that answer the question.

notFromPassage.title: Words not from the passage
notFromPassage.count: {count} of {total} typed answers used a word that is not in the passage (questions {numbers})
notFromPassage.tip: When the instruction says <en>from the passage</en>, write the passage's own words, even if you know a synonym.

pins.title: Pins differed from the cited evidence
pins.count: {count} of {total} questions with pinned sentences: none of the pins was a sentence the key cites (questions {numbers})
pins.tip: Compare your pinned sentence with the sentence the review cites. Look for the same idea in the passage, not only the same words.

paraphrase.title: Questions that use other words
paraphrase.count: {count} of {total} questions that say the passage's idea in other words were not fully correct (questions {numbers})
paraphrase.tip: Look for the same idea, not the same words. In the review, compare the question's words with the evidence.

qualifier.title: Questions that turn on a small word
qualifier.count: {count} of {total} questions that turn on a word like <en>all</en>, <en>most</en> or <en>only</en> were not fully correct (questions {numbers})
qualifier.tip: Check words such as <en>all</en>, <en>most</en>, <en>some</en>, <en>only</en>, <en>always</en> and <en>never</en> in both the question and the passage.
